task.name: Flaky Test Quarantine Review
task.description: Review tests in covered repositories that fail non-deterministically in at least three default-branch runs within 14 days, then surface only recurrent candidates that are not already quarantined, fixed, or tracked with equivalent evidence.
task.intent: Reduce maintainer time spent identifying recurrent flaky tests that warrant bounded quarantine review while requiring accepted repository evidence for every resolved candidate.
activationConditions: The same test identity has a failing result and a passing result on the same default-branch commit, or fails and later passes without a test-affecting change, in at least three runs during the 14-day evidence window.
Repository evidence does not already show an active quarantine, merged fix, or open equivalent tracking record for that test identity.
requiredEffects: Each novel finding identifies one stable test identity, the recurrent contradictory run evidence, affected workflow, recurrence window, and the absence of an equivalent quarantine or tracking record.

Each surfaced candidate remains review-only and can be resolved only through repository-linked evidence that a maintainer accepted a bounded quarantine, accepted a verified fix, or explicitly dismissed the recurrence evidence.
noopConditions: No test identity satisfies the recurrence threshold with contradictory default-branch run evidence in the 14-day window.
Every supported recurrent candidate is already quarantined, fixed, or represented by an equivalent open tracking record.
successConditions: Supported novel candidates receive accepted resolution evidence or an explicit maintainer dismissal within 14 days of the workflow run.
Tests below the recurrence threshold and already tracked candidates create no duplicate maintainer attention.
uncertainties: Renamed or parameterized tests may prevent reliable stable-identity matching across runs.
Infrastructure-wide failures can mimic test-level flakiness and require maintainer dismissal rather than quarantine.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported novel recurrent flaky-test quarantine candidates assigned to the run that receive accepted resolution evidence or explicit maintainer dismissal within 14 days.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported recurrent flaky-test quarantine candidates it assigns from the bounded 14-day default-branch evidence window.
acceptedEvidence: A merged pull request that identifies the test and either adds a bounded quarantine with owner, expiry condition, and linked follow-up record, or applies a fix followed by a passing default-branch run for the previously failing test.

A repository issue or pull-request review record in which a maintainer explicitly dismisses the candidate as unsupported, duplicate, or infrastructure-caused and links the evaluated recurrence evidence.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran and in which the identified test and accepted resolution record reside.

metric.name: accepted-resolution-flaky-test-quarantine-candidates
metric.formula: supported novel recurrent flaky-test quarantine candidates with accepted resolution evidence or explicit maintainer dismissal / supported novel recurrent flaky-test quarantine candidates assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 14 days after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel recurrent flaky-test quarantine candidate was assigned and none has accepted resolution evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned candidate set, stable test identity, required default-branch run evidence, or repository-linked resolution evidence cannot be read.

rows.finding-summary: tests/cache.test.js::reuses-entry failed and passed on the same revision in three default-branch runs within 14 days; no quarantine, fix, or equivalent issue exists.

rows.outcome-summary: Maintainer accepted a bounded quarantine with owner, expiry condition, and linked follow-up.
